name: crew
description: Makes the main session a lead that delegates to six specialist subagents: code-reader and research on Haiku; designer, developer and tester on Sonnet; architect on Opus. It also shows a live dashboard of the session (Flightdeck, vendored). With the jevKey option set (a TypeSafe key), Jev may move each call's model one step (the architect stays on Opus) and raise its effort to high, and it sizes the effort of each Codex job; that sends a redacted, truncated prompt to api.typesafe.ai. With the codex option on, the lead can run a role on OpenAI Codex through the local Codex CLI, which sends the prompt and the repository content the job reads to OpenAI. With the nativeCodex option set and a local proxy as ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, roles also get crew:<role>-codex subagent types that run on a Codex model through that proxy.

jevKey.title: Jev API key (TypeSafe)
jevKey.description: Setting this key turns Jev routing on; leaving it empty turns it off. With a key, Jev (TypeSafe) chooses the model and effort of each crew:* Agent call, one step from the agent's default and never below the architect's Opus floor or medium effort, and the choice shows in the task's description. The call's description and its prompt (secrets and paths removed, cut to 4000 characters) are sent to api.typesafe.ai. When the Codex engine is on, Jev also sets each Codex job's effort (medium or high, never the model) and the job's description and redacted prompt are sent there too. The agent type is never changed, and a call that names a model keeps it. The key is sent only in the Authorization header and is never logged or stored by the plugin. A repository's own settings cannot supply it.

codex.title: Codex engine
codex.description: Lets the lead run a crew role on OpenAI Codex through the local Codex CLI instead of a Claude subagent. When on, the prompts the lead writes and the repository content the job reads are sent to OpenAI by that CLI, under your Codex login and plan. The crew's Write and Edit guard does not apply to Codex jobs. Jobs run on medium effort unless Jev raises them to high, so the model_reasoning_effort in your Codex config.toml no longer applies to them. Off by default; when off, nothing is registered or run.

codexModels.title: Codex models per role
codexModels.description: Optional Codex model for each role, as role=model pairs separated by commas, e.g. developer=gpt-x,architect=gpt-y. Roles left out use Codex's own default model. Only used when the Codex engine is on.

nativeCodex.title: Native Codex models per role
nativeCodex.description: Registers a crew:<role>-codex subagent type for each role=model pair, e.g. developer=gpt-x,tester=gpt-y, running on that model with the role's prompt, tools and write lane. The model is reached through a local proxy at ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, so the types are registered only when that URL is an http URL on a loopback address (127.0.0.0/8, ::1 or localhost); with any other base URL, or none, nothing is registered. What those subagents read and write is sent to OpenAI through the proxy. Jev routing leaves them alone. Empty by default.

architectPattern.title: Architect pattern
architectPattern.description: Regular expression (case-insensitive) for the agent types and server tools that count as the on-call architect, e.g. advisor|architect|reviewer

architectLabel.title: Architect label
architectLabel.description: Name shown for the architect role

gateLabel.title: Gate label
gateLabel.description: Name shown for the permission panel

panels.title: Panels
panels.description: Comma-separated panels in display order: main, architect, gate, agents, loops, receipt, log. Leave one out to hide it.

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: Animate the connectors while real work flows, or keep them still

moments.title: Architect moments
moments.description: Show the inferred moment of each consult (before a plan, error repeats, before done)

matchDescriptions.title: Match agent descriptions
matchDescriptions.description: Also count an agent type as the architect when its description (not just its name) matches the pattern

maxCards.title: Cards before swimlanes
maxCards.description: Agent cards drawn side by side; more agents than this switch to swimlanes (1-6)

layout.title: Layout
layout.description: Layout of the side pane. auto: a summary of at most 8 rows when the pane sits inline above the prompt, two columns from 110 columns when docked, one column otherwise. /crew:panel layout changes it for the session; the prompt band always shows the summary

palette.title: Palette
palette.description: theme follows your Claude Code theme (light, dark, colour-blind); pastel is fixed colours tuned for dark terminals

openOnStart.title: Open on start
openOnStart.description: Show the panel when a session starts and you have not picked yet with /crew:panel; once you have, your pick wins

placement.title: Placement
placement.description: Where the panel shows before you pick with /crew:panel. side: the pane beside the transcript (inline above the prompt on a narrow terminal or the main screen). prompt: a summary band above the prompt, which yields to any other plugin's band (terminal and desktop only)

statusLine.title: Status line
statusLine.description: Show context, agents, consults and denials in the status line
